svg.title: LXC-CH347 (CH347T board) in mode 1: the headers
svg.text: LXC-CH347 (CH347T board) in mode 1: the headers
Top view, USB-C down. Each pin: its silkscreen, the back's IO label where it has one, its function in mode 1, its pins() name.
same chip pin as another header
S1 on, S2 off: mode 1, USB ID 1a86:55db (UART1 + I2C + SPI)
Set it unplugged: the chip reads it at power-up.
• The UART0 and JTAG headers carry the same chip pins as the SPI and I2C headers (dashed).
• Wire to the SPI and I2C headers, and leave the dashed ones free: a wire there sits on the bus too.
• The back prints IO0-IO7, but only IO4, IO6 and IO7 are GPIOs here (WCH's driver); the others are SPI's and I2C's.
• GPIO4 and GPIO6 serve as digital I/O or as chip selects. GPIO7 (UART1 RTS) is the mode switch's pin (S1): leave it to the switch.
• CS0 and CS1 are the SPI's chip selects, output only: one not selecting a device is a digital output (pins({ CS1: true })).
• UART1 (TX, RX) is the serial port, ttyACM on Linux. 5V is USB's, 3V3 the board's 3.3 V: power 3.3 V parts from it.

Headers from the vendor's photos, front and back; chip pins from the silkscreen names and WCH CH347DS1 V1.6 (§4.3), borne out by the back's IO labels; GPIOs per WCH's Linux driver. atiic docs/ch347.md.
